issues: The summary says only that Article 16 was "added to". It leaves out what new clause (4B) does: reserved vacancies left unfilled can be carried forward and do not count toward the fifty per cent ceiling of the later year.

proposed_one_liner: Added Article 16(4B), which lets reserved vacancies left unfilled in a year be carried forward to later years. These carried-forward vacancies do not count toward the fifty per cent limit on reservation for the later year.

proposed_one_liner: Changed the First Schedule to carry out the 1974 land boundary agreement with Bangladesh and its 2011 protocol, under which the two countries exchanged enclaves. The changes are to the territories of Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.

issues: The summary only says Articles 15 and 16 were "added to". It leaves out the main change: up to ten per cent reservation in education and public jobs for economically weaker sections who are outside the existing reserved groups.
evidence: 103.txt p.1-2: "(6) Nothing in this article or sub-clause (g) of clause (1) of article 19 or clause (2) of article 29 shall prevent the State from making,— (a) any special provision for the advancement of any economically weaker sections of citizens other than the classes mentioned in clauses (4) and (5); and (b) ... admission to educational institutions including private educational institutions ... subject to a maximum of ten per cent. of the total seats in each category."; art. 16 "(6) ... reservation of appointments or posts in favour of any economically weaker sections of citizens other than the classes mentioned in clause (4), in addition to the existing reservation and subject to a maximum of ten per cent. of the posts in each category." Constitution_of_India_10.9.2026.pdf.txt l.1296, 1376: "(w.e.f. 14-1-2019)". Date is right.
proposed_one_liner: Added Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) for economically weaker sections of citizens who are not in the groups that already have reservation. The State may reserve up to ten per cent of seats in educational institutions and of posts in public employment for them, on top of existing reservations.

issues: The summary leaves out a major change. The Act extended reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (clause (a)) to eighty years, but kept seventy years for nominating Anglo-Indian members (clause (b)), so that nomination ended on 25 January 2020.
evidence: 104.txt p.1-2: "(2) It shall come into force on the 25th day of January, 2020."; "(b) in the long line, after clauses (a) and (b), for the words \"seventy years\", the words \"eighty years in respect of clause (a) and seventy years in respect of clause (b)\" shall be substituted." Constitution_of_India_10.9.2026.pdf.txt l.8669: "Subs. by the Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019, s. 2, for \"seventy years\" (w.e.f. 25-1-2020)." Date is right.
proposed_one_liner: Extended reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Article 334 from seventy to eighty years, and replaced its heading. It kept the seventy-year limit for nominated Anglo-Indian members, so their nomination ended in January 2020.

issues: The summary names the Articles but leaves out the main change: the President's list of socially and educationally backward classes became a "Central List" for the Central Government only, and every State and Union territory may make its own list by law.
evidence: 105.pdf p.1: "(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may ... appoint" (assent "[18th August, 2021.]"); p.2: s.2 adds to 338B(9) "Provided that nothing in this clause shall apply for the purposes of clause (3) of article 342A."; s.3 "the socially and educationally backward classes in the Central List which shall for the purposes of the Central Government" and "(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in clauses (1) and (2), every State or Union territory may, by law, prepare and maintain, for its own purposes, a list of socially and educationally backward classes, entries in which may be different from the Central List."; s.4 substitutes 366(26C). Constitution_of_India_10.9.2026.pdf.txt l.8980, 9063: "(w.e.f. 15-9-2021)". Date is right.
proposed_one_liner: Changed Articles 338B, 342A and 366(26C) so that the President's list of socially and educationally backward classes is a Central List, used by the Central Government. Each State and Union territory may make its own list by law, which can differ from the Central List.

issues: The summary says the reservation starts after "the first census after 2023". The Act says the first census taken after the Act comes into force, which the edition gives as 16 April 2026, so "after 2023" is wrong.
evidence: 106.txt p.2: "334A. (1) ... shall come into effect after an exercise of delimitation is undertaken for this purpose after the relevant figures for the first census taken after commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 have been published and shall cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of fifteen years from such commencement. (2) ... shall continue till such date as the Parliament may by law determine." s.1(2): "It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint." Constitution_of_India_10.9.2026.pdf.txt l.5531, 8502, 8589, 8677: "(w.e.f. 16-4-2026)". Date 16 April 2026 is right for the Act itself.
proposed_one_liner: Added Articles 330A, 332A and 334A, reserving about one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, and added the same for the Delhi Assembly to Article 239AA. The reservation starts only after the first census taken after the Act came into force and a fresh delimitation based on it, and lasts fifteen years unless Parliament extends it.
